newsitem.title: UK: LME copper hits seven-week high above $2,000.
newsitem.headline: LME copper hits seven-week high above $2,000.

text.p: Three month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange (LME) broke above the $2,000-a-tonne barrier for the first time in seven weeks late on Thursday, up from $1,993 at Thursday's afternoon kerb close.
Traders attributed the rise to short-covering and expectations of another hefty drawdown in LME inventories in Friday's data.
Stocks have fallen over 115,000 tonnes in under two months. On Thursday they stood at a 14-month low of 159,350 tonnes.

The metal was mostly coming out of European warehouses and moving to various ports in China, to end-users in Europe and to the Middle East, physical traders said. If the stock drawdowns continued, prices could shoot higher still, they added.
But liquidation, producer sales and traders protecting short positions were keeping pressure on the market, traders said.
At 1731 GMT three month copper futures were quoted at $2,003/05 a tonne. The next big target was pegged at $2,070.
